newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian police investigating break-in at ASC.
newsitem.headline: Australian police investigating break-in at ASC.

text.p: Police are looking into a reported break-in at Australian Securities Commission offices which a newspaper has linked to an ongoing investigation into dealings in shares of Coles Myer Ltd.

"The Australian Federal Police can confirm that we are undertaking initial inquiries into a reported incident at the offices of the Australian Securities Commission," police spokesman Keith Livingston told Reuters on Tuesday.
"As those inquiries are ongoing it would be inappropriate to make any further comment," he said.

Melbourne's Herald Sun newspaper said intruders broke into the ASC's Melbourne offices over the weekend to "spy" on documents relating to the Coles Myer, Australia's largest retailing group. "They ignored money, valuables and unlocked doors and made for the 'Coles Myer room'," the newspaper said.

The locked room contained sensitive documents concerning the so-called Yannon transaction, a 1990 deal which cost the Coles Myer group A$18 million and benefitted a company associated with Coles Myer's former chairman Solomon Lew by a similar amount.
The break-in was discovered by staff on Monday morning, the newspaper said. The ASC said it had no immediate comment.
